newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Oil shares rise on Nigerian bourse.
newsitem.headline: Oil shares rise on Nigerian bourse.

text.p: Oil shares firmed on the Nigerian Stock market on Thursday after unsteady trade earlier in the week on fears of weak trading results, dealers said.
The all-share index rose 16.43 points to 6634.78 from 6618.35 on Wednesday.
Strong activity in the oil sector resumed after another major marketer released a slightly improved half-year result contrary to what was widely expected.
Unipetrol said its net profit to end-June 1996 was 339.9 million naira against 301 million naira in the same six-month period in 1995.
"Shareholders' expectations would continue to be met in the remaining part of the year, barring any unforseen contingency," Unipetrol said in a statement to stock traders.
"It was a modest improvement but the delay in presenting the results got worried brokers to anticipate a spate of poor performances," one broker said.
Unipetrol rose one naira to close at 45.50 naira on Thursday.
Total, which reported lower profit on Monday, also rose 80 kobo to 50.00 naira. National Oil added 60 kobo to 37.80 naira while Mobil was 45 kobo up at 42.40 naira.
Nestle Foods ended 40 kobo up at 38.50 naira while Union Dicon Salt finished 30 kobo stronger at 38.00 naira on sustained investors interest.
Guinness fell 20 kobo to 7.00 naira for lack of interest, the same as NAL Merchant Bank which ended at 5.20 naira.
Union Bank, UAC and Abatex each dropped five kobo to close respectively at 7.35 naira, 9.45 naira and 4.05 naira.
